video_title: Who Will Be KEY Players At NBA Trade Deadline?

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Orlando Magic's roster challenges and potential luxury tax implications
quotes.excerpt: It's an expensive roster to be seven and nine, especially a team that's fought to get into play.
quotes.quote: I just wrote Orlando, which I'm really interested with them where they are. I think they were seven and nine as of Monday. Just can't find their footing. They've had injuries again with Banchero, and Suggs comes back. It's an expensive roster to be seven and nine, especially a team that's fought to get into play in the last couple years, and it's going to get more expensive if they retain Anthony Black, who's a restricted free agent. And as you guys know, when you're paying the luxury tax, first time they paid the luxury tax in like 20 years, most expensive tax bill they've had in franchise history here. I think teams like that, Orlando is intriguing, just the expectations when you have a big payroll like that.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Anthony Black's contract situation and potential trade considerations for Orlando
quotes.excerpt: Is he going to be too expensive for the Magic to keep him?

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: Orlando is really interesting to me. You mentioned Anthony Black, and it's one of those things of is he going to be too expensive for the Magic to keep him? If that's the case, are you better off trading him now, getting first-round compensation in return, or do you play it out in the restricted free agency, which is dicey because there are a lot of teams that are going to have cap space? Or do you try to move somebody now to make room on the payroll to pay Anthony Black?

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: So that that one is fascinating.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Franz Wagner's breakout season and increased role for Orlando
quotes.excerpt: Franz Wagner is having an interesting year, guys. He is averaging eight assists per game.
quotes.quote: The interesting thing about what's going on in Orlando right now, so Paolo Banchero has been out for almost the entire season, and Jalen Suggs has been out for a bunch of the season. He continues to have injury problems. So their team morphed a little bit and is playing more Anthony Black and basically playing through Franz Wagner more. And the interesting thing is that Wagner is having an interesting year, guys. He is averaging eight assists per game. It's probably a little bit higher than that since Banchero went out. Last year he averaged three. His career average is just a little under four. He is averaging eight assists a game. He's playing point forward for them, the role that Paolo plays. The second thing is he has been a terror driving the ball.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeff Weltman's comments on the end of the Magic's continuity
quotes.excerpt: The continuity thing is not going to continue next year.
quotes.quote: I was looking at some quotes from before the season started, Jeff Weltman, their head of basketball operations. I think it was media day and he says, listen, the continuity thing is not going to continue next year, right? Like eventually we're going to have to make some pretty tough decisions here. And they hired Sean Sweeney. I'm sure you guys saw the clip of Sweeney, what the Sweeney, I guess lit into him a little bit in that huddle there in the market went blind.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Sean Sweeney's viral huddle rant and clipboard slam
quotes.excerpt: It was a good rant and a great clipboard slam.
quotes.quote: It was a good rant and a great clipboard slam. I mean the punctuation at the end was really strong. And Sweeney's, you know, he's a fine little leprechaun, so his face got as red as his hair. It was great.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Suggs' high school football background and athletic career
quotes.excerpt: Jalen Suggs, I believe, is the best high school football player in the NBA today.
quotes.quote: By the way, Jalen Suggs, I believe, is the best high school football player in the NBA today. He had the best high school football career of any active NBA player. LeBron was awesome. Jalen Suggs was a dual-threat quarterback and elite safety in Mr. Football, Minnesota. And he had offers from like Ohio State, Georgia, I mean like that kind of list. Anyways.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: New Orleans Pelicans' struggles and potential trade deadline activity
quotes.excerpt: New Orleans is going to be a team we'll be watching just based on their performance.
quotes.quote: You look at the standings, of course, New Orleans is going to be a team we'll be watching just based on their performance. I think they're one and nine in their last 10, and of course, the Dejounte Murray situation there.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Brooklyn Nets' disappointing performance and trade deadline outlook
quotes.excerpt: Brooklyn is going to be fascinating, where they are with Cam Thomas and Julius Randle.
quotes.quote: I think Brooklyn is going to be fascinating, where they are with Cam Thomas and Julius Randle, especially after that Chicago game last week, which was one of the worst games I've seen. They were embarrassing, and they were more competitive in the Orlando game. They lose on a Franz shot at the end. That was funny. I was watching the end of the, so I didn't even mention that Franz hit a game-winner with like two seconds left.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Los Angeles Clippers' trade deadline potential and expiring contracts
quotes.excerpt: The Clippers are going to be interesting. All those expiring contracts and everything like that.
quotes.quote: The Clippers are going to be interesting. I think Clippers are going to be interesting. All those expiring contracts and everything like that. But yeah, we'll have all those free agents that signed. Most of the free agents that signed deals get their trade restriction gets lifted on December 15th, and it just kind of opens up the playing field for for more deals.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Indiana Pacers' disappointing season and trade deadline expectations

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: Bobby, let me throw one at you. What about Indiana, who kind of came out of nowhere and made a big trade last year?

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: I put the, I put the mush on that team, man. I apologize to Pacer fans because I was talking up them something terrific during the off-season. And they basically returned all those guys from that team that went to the finals. Yeah, that's a great point. It's like they're almost like Orlando a little bit. I think they are like Orlando, you know, as far as the continuity part of it. And you have a lot of, you've got they had a lot of guys this off-season who were extension eligible, nobody got one. You have Siakam going into the last year of his deal next year. Haliburton still got a bunch of years left, but like Nembhard, Niche Smith, Toppin, Zubac, that trade is, you know, at best, you know, the jury is still out on that trade. They're expensive. They're a tax team here and as of Monday, I think they're five and 12, something like that, somewhere around there. So yeah, that would be a team, usually they're more of like the aggressor, I would say, but it's would be interesting if they if they're kind of selling off some, you know, if they're looking at maybe reducing some payroll there.
